articles.text: Parliament shall have full control over publ finance. No tax, rate or any other levy shall be imposed b any local authority or any other public authority, exce by or under the authority of a law passed by Parliament of any existing law.

The interest on the public debt, sinking fun payments, the costs, charges and expenses incidental the collection, management and receipt of the Consolidate Fund and such other expenditure as Parliament ma determine shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund.

No such warrant shall be issued unless th sum has by resolution of Parliament or by any law bee granted for specified public services for the financi year during which the withdrawal is to take place or otherwise lawfully, charged on the Consolidated Fund.

Where the President dissolves Parliament befo the Appropriation Bill for the financial year has passe into law, he may, unless Parliament shall have alread made provision, authorize the issue from the Consolidate Fund and the expenditure of such sums as he ma consider necessary for the public services until the expir titution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka of a period of three months from the date on which the new Parliament is summoned to meet.

Where the President dissolves Parliament and ixes a date or dates for a General Election the President may, unless Parliament has already made provision in that behalf, authorize the issue from the Consolidated Fund and he expenditure of such sums as he may, after consultation with the Commissioner of Elections, consider necessary or such elections.
Notwithstanding any of the provisions of Article 149, Parliament may by law create a Contingencies Fund for the purpose of providing for urgent and unforeseen expenditure.

The Minister in charge of the subject of Finance, f satisfied – (a) that there is need for any such expenditure; and (b) that no provision for such expenditure exists, may, with the consent of the President, authorize provision to be made therefore by an advance from the Contingencies Fund.
As soon as possible after every such advance, a Supplementary Estimate shall be presented to Parliament or the purpose of replacing the amount so advanced.

articles.text: No Bill or motion, authorizing the disposal of, or he imposition of charges upon, the Consolidated Fund or other funds of the Republic, or the imposition of any tax or he repeal, augmentation or reduction of any tax for the ime being in force shall be introduced in Parliament except by a Minister, and unless such Bill or motion has been approved either by the Cabinet of Ministers or in such manner as the Cabinet of Ministers may authorize.

clauses.text: There shall be an Auditor-General wh shall be a qualified Auditor, and who shall subject t the approval of the Constitutional Council, be appointe by the President. The Auditor-General shall hold offic during good behaviour.
The salary of the Auditor-General shall b determined by Parliament, shall be charged on th Consolidated Fund and shall not be diminished during hi term of office.

The office of the Auditor-General shall becom vacant - (a) upon his death; (b) on his resignation in writing addressed to th President; (c) on his attaining the age of sixty years; (d) on his removal by the President on account o ill health or physical or mental infirmity; or (e) on his removal by the President upon a address of Parliament.

Whenever the Auditor-General is unable t discharge the functions of his office, the President may subject to the approval of the Constitutional Council appoint a qualified auditor to act in the place of th Auditor-General.

clauses.text: There shall be an Audit Servic Commission (in this Chapter referred to as the "Commission" which shall consist of the Auditor-General who sha be the Chairman of the Commission, and the followin titution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka members appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Constitutional Council:- (a) two retired officers of the Auditor-General's Department, who have held office as a Deputy Auditor-General or above; (b) a retired judge of the Supreme Court, the Court of Appeal or the High Court of Sri Lanka; and (c) a retired Class I officer of the Sri Lanka Administrative Service.

A person appointed as a member of the Commission shall hold office for three years, unless he - (a) earlier resigns from his office, by letter addressed to the President; (b) is removed from office as hereinafter provided; or (c) becomes a Member of Parliament or a member of a Provincial Council or a local authority.
A person appointed as a member of the Commission shall be eligible to be appointed for a further term of office, on the recommendation of the Constitutional Council.
The President may, for cause assigned and with the approval of the Constitutional Council, remove from office any person appointed as a member of the Commission under paragraph (1).

The Chairman and the members of the Commission shall be paid such allowances as are determined by Parliament. Such allowances shall be charged on the Consolidated Fund and shall not be diminished during the term of office of the Chairman o members.
The Chairman and the members of th Commission shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning and for the purposes of Chapter IX of th Penal Code (Chapter 19).
There shall be a Secretary to the Commission who shall be appointed by the Commission.

articles.description: Powers and functions of the Commission

clauses.text: The powers of appointment, promotion transfer, disciplinary control and dismissal of th members belonging to the Sri Lanka State Audit Service shall be vested in the Commission.

The Commission shall also exercise, perform and discharge the following powers, duties and functions:- (a) make rules pertaining to schemes o recruitment, the appointment, transfer disciplinary control and dismissal of th members belonging to the Sri Lanka Stat Audit Service, subject to any policy determined by the Cabinet of Minister pertaining to the same; (b) prepare annual estimates of the Nationa Audit Office established by law; and (c) exercise, perform and discharge such othe powers, duties and functions as may b provided for by law. titution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
The Commission shall cause the rules made under paragraph
to be published in the Gazette.
Every such rule shall come into operation on the date of such publication or on such later date as may be specified in such rule.

Every such rule shall, within three months of such publication in the Gazette be brought before Parliament for approval. Any rule which is not so approved shall be deemed to be rescinded as from the date of such disapproval, but without prejudice to anything previously done thereunder.

articles.description: Influencing or attempting to influence decision of the Commission or any officer of the Sri Lanka State Audit Service, to be an offence

clauses.text: A person who otherwise than in the course of his duty, directly or indirectly, by himself or through any other person, in any manner whatsoever, influences or attempts to influence any decision of the Commission, any member thereof or any officer of the Sri Lanka State Audit Service, commits an offence and shall on conviction be liable to a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or to both such fine and imprisonment.
Every High Court established under Article 154P of the Constitution shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine any matter referred to in paragraph (1).

articles.text: Subject to the jurisdiction conferred on the Supreme Court under Article 126 and to the powers granted to the Administrative Appeals Tribunal under Article 153G, no court or tribunal shall have the power or jurisdiction to inquire into, pronounce upon or in any manner whatsoever call in question any order or decision made by the Commission, in pursuance of any function assigned to such Commission under this Chapter or under any law.
The costs and expenses of the Commissio shall be a charge on the Consolidated Fund.

articles.description: Appeals to the Administrative Appeals Tribunal
articles.text: Any officer of the Sri Lanka State Aud Service who is aggrieved by any order relating to th appointment, promotion or transfer of such officer or an order on a disciplinary matter or dismissal made by th Commission, in respect of such officer, may appe therefrom to the Administrative Appeals Tribun established under Article 59, which shall have the power t alter, vary, rescind or confirm any order or decision mad by the Commission.

articles.description: Commission to be answerable to Parliament
articles.text: The Commission shall be responsible an answerable to Parliament in accordance with th provisions of the Standing Orders of Parliament for th discharge of its functions and shall forward to Parliamen in each calendar year a report of its activities in such year

Where such appointment has been made by the Minister, the Auditor-General may, in writing, inform such auditor or auditors that he proposes to utilize his or their services for the performance and discharge of the Auditor-General’s duties and functions in relation to such public corporation, business or other undertaking or a company referred to in paragraph
and thereupon such auditor or auditors shall act under the direction and control of the Auditor-General.
The Auditor-General shall also perform and discharge such duties and functions as may be prescribed by Parliament by law.

(a) The Auditor-General may for the purpose of the performance and discharge of his duties and functions engage the services of a qualified auditor or auditors who shall act under his direction and control. (b) If the Auditor-General is of opinion that it is necessary to obtain assistance in the examination of any technical, professional or scientific problem relevant to the audit, he may engage the services of – (i) a person not being an employee of the department, body or authority the accounts of which are being audited, or by the Nineteenth Amendment to the Constitution Sec. 36(2). by the Nineteenth Amendment to the Constitution Sec. 36(2). by the Nineteenth Amendment to the Constitution Sec. 36(2). (ii) any technical or professional or scientifi institution not being an institution which has any interest in the management o the affairs of such department, body o authority, and such person or institution shall act under his direction and control.

(a) The Auditor-General or any person authorized by him shall in the performance and discharge of his duties and functions be entitled – (i) to have access to all books, records returns and other documents; (ii) to have access to stores and othe property; and (iii) to be furnished with such information and explanations as may be necessary fo the performance of such duties and functions. (b) Every qualified auditor appointed to audi the accounts of any public corporation, business o other undertaking or a company referred to in paragraph (1), or any person authorized by such auditor shall b entitled to like access, information and explanations in relation to such public corporation, business or othe undertaking or a company referred to in paragraph (1).

The Auditor-General shall within ten month after the close of each financial year and as and when h deems it necessary report to Parliament on th performance and, discharge of his duties and function under the Constitution. titution of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka

In this Article, “qualified auditor” means – (a) an individual who, being a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka, or of any other Institute established by law, possesses a certificate to practise as an Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute; or (b) firm of Accountants each of the resident partners of which, being a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka or of any other Institute established by law, possesses a certificate to practise as an Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute.
